summary_paragraph: A male patient with Factor V Leiden and a known aortic arch thrombus was readmitted for persistent pleuritic chest pain and hemoptysis. Imaging showed the aortic thrombus was slightly smaller with no extension or new pulmonary embolism, indicating stability on anticoagulation with Lovenox. The chest pain was deemed likely musculoskeletal, related to recent coughing from bronchitis. Hemoptysis had decreased in volume and was not from active bleeding. Chronic abdominal pain and blood in stool were noted but without acute findings. Pain management was adjusted with cautious use of Dilaudid, and anxiety was addressed with continued venlafaxine and a clonazepam taper. A complex renal cyst was identified, requiring ultrasound follow-up in six months. The patient was discharged after 24 hours with plans for ongoing specialty follow-up and primary care coordination.
